subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs implicitly clean up their run sessions, or should recurring jobs reject `deleteAfterRun` and use a different recovery path?
rationale: Two open PRs encode opposite public cron lifecycle contracts, and choosing incorrectly can either leave the token-leak upgrade path open or break previously accepted recurring cron shapes.

options.title: Adopt recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this direction, but require persisted-upgrade handling and tests for existing omitted `deleteAfterRun` jobs before merge.

options.title: Adopt one-shot-only rejection
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation path after Gateway, UI, and recovery gaps are fixed.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only behavior
options.body: Land this as a narrow default change while explicitly documenting that existing omitted jobs need operator action or separate migration.

recommendation.title: Adopt recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this direction, but require persisted-upgrade handling and tests for existing omitted `deleteAfterRun` jobs before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger is the strongest current-history owner for the cron normalization and persisted-store paths where the contract choice lands.
